explanations: luna: People are described as dead, given life, made to die, then restored to life; this gives the section's movement from burial to new creation a direct formulation. | terra: People were dead, are given life, will die, and will be brought back; the verse states the full transformation behind the section's grave-and-new-creation layer.
luna: Adam and his wife are sent down and given an earthly dwelling and provision for a time; this is another account of the section's garden-to-need transition.
luna: Adam receives words from his Lord and is forgiven; this supplies a second formulation of loss followed by divine turning.

luna: The descent is followed by a promise that guidance will come and that followers of it need not fear or grieve; this specifies the sheltering effect of guidance. | terra: In the other Adam descent account, guidance is promised after the fall, and its followers need not fear or grieve; it confirms the same fall-then-guidance structure as 20:123.
terra: Israel is reminded of deliverance from Pharaoh's people, who slaughtered sons and spared women; rescued vulnerable children form an earlier divine favor meant to be remembered.
luna: Moses strikes a rock and twelve springs flow, with each group knowing its drinking place; this repeats water provision in Moses's story alongside the section's flock at the well.

luna: The covenant pairs kindness to orphans and needy people with speaking well to others; it brings the section's care of vulnerable people together with its rule for speech. | terra: The covenant joins kindness to parents, relatives, orphans, and the needy with speaking good to people; remembered nurture, vulnerable recipients, and gentle voice are one duty.

luna: The verse says that one who exchanges faith for disbelief has strayed from the straight way; it makes the section's lost-route image a chosen departure from guidance, not only not knowing a direction.

luna: Righteousness includes giving wealth to orphans, needy people, travelers, and those who ask, as well as freeing captives; the verse gathers the section's vulnerable recipients. | terra: Righteousness includes giving loved wealth to relatives, orphans, the needy, travelers, and askers; several recipients of the section's final commands are gathered under one giving act.

luna: Asked what to spend, the answer names parents, relatives, orphans, needy people, and travelers; it gives the asker a concrete answer centered on care. | terra: The answer about spending names parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and travelers; received good is routed toward both those who raised a person and those now dependent on him.

luna: Asked about orphans, the answer says reforming their affairs is best and that sharing life with them makes them brothers; this gives the section's sheltering image a kinship ethic. | terra: Questions about orphans are answered that setting their affairs right is best and mixing with them makes them brothers; guardianship is reforming fellowship rather than possession.

terra: Nursing, a father's duty to provide, protection of both parents from harm, mutually willing consultation, and paid foster nursing all meet in one child-rearing rule; it supplies the consensual household structure behind Moses's nursing scene.
luna: The verse says there is no compulsion in religion and distinguishes guidance from error; it marks a boundary between being guided and forcing another.

luna: God brings believers from darkness into light, while false guardians bring others from light back into darkness; this gives the section's light-and-guidance meeting a reversal. | terra: God as guardian brings believers from darkness into light, while false patrons reverse the movement; ownership and illumination are joined through the identity of the true guardian.
luna: A man and his ruined town ask how God will revive it after its death; the man is made to die and restored, a concrete sign of new creation.
luna: Abraham asks to see how God gives life to the dead, and is shown birds reassembled and summoned; this makes the section's buried-to-new-creation image visible.
terra: Those who spend and do not follow their gifts with reminders or injury receive security from their Lord; the verse protects the receiver from the giver's later verbal qahr.

luna: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury; this directly contrasts the section's giving with harm in speech. | terra: A kind word and forgiveness are declared better than charity followed by hurt; this directly joins the giving hand to the gentle voice that must accompany it.

luna: The verse warns that reminders and injury can nullify charity; it places a boundary on speaking about a gift that fits the section's command to tell blessing. | terra: Charity is invalidated by reminders of generosity and hurt; this limits public speech about favor so that the giver does not turn gift into domination of its recipient.

luna: Satan threatens poverty, while God promises forgiveness and bounty; this counters the fear of need that the section answers with future provision. | terra: Satan threatens poverty, while God promises forgiveness and bounty; fear of future need is directly answered by trust in future divine giving.

luna: Giving openly is good, while giving secretly to the poor may be better; this sets a context-sensitive boundary on the section's command to make blessing known. | terra: Disclosing charity is good, while concealing it for the poor is better; it marks the boundary between openly recounting God's favor and protecting a recipient through hidden giving.

luna: The poor are described as restrained and not importuning people, though an uninformed observer may think them self-sufficient; this adds hidden need to the section's visible asker. | terra: Restrained poor people may be mistaken for self-sufficient because they do not beg insistently; it makes hidden need the test of a giver who sees beyond the audible request.
terra: Those who spend by night and day, secretly and openly, carry provision through every light and disclosure state named by the section.
terra: A debtor in hardship must be given time until ease, while remitting the debt is better; delay becomes mercy directed toward another person's insufficiency.

terra: Mary's Lord causes her to grow well, places her in Zakariyya's care, and he repeatedly finds provision with her; رب, guardianship, finding, growth, and provision converge in one dependent child's scene.

luna: The Prophet's gentleness is attributed to God's mercy, and harshness is said to drive people away; this shows what a soft response preserves against rebuke. | terra: The Prophet's divinely given gentleness keeps people near, whereas harshness and hardness of heart would scatter them; soft voice and receptive heart are causally joined.

luna: Guardians are commanded to give orphans their property and not consume or exchange it wrongly; this specifies how a caretaker must not take from the vulnerable. | terra: Guardians must hand orphans their property and not consume it by substitution; it states the section's concrete prohibition on a stronger hand taking from an orphan.
luna: The verse tells guardians who fear injustice toward orphan girls to marry other women; it makes fairness in a household the boundary around the section's orphan-and-marriage images.
terra: Those managing property must provide food and clothing from it and speak a fitting word; material care and gentle speech are one guardianship duty.

luna: Guardians must test orphans until maturity and then hand over their property, with limits on a poor guardian's use; the verse makes care temporary and accountable. | terra: Orphans are tested until maturity, then their property is handed over with witnesses, while rich guardians abstain and poor ones take only fairly; nurture, consent, and limits replace qahr.

luna: When relatives, orphans, and needy people attend an inheritance distribution, they are to receive provision and kind words; this joins the section's hand and voice. | terra: When orphans and the needy attend a distribution, they are to receive something and be addressed with a fitting word; hand and voice jointly protect the excluded.
luna: Those who consume orphan property unjustly are said to consume fire; this gives a severe boundary to the section's ban on crushing the orphan.

luna: Property may pass between people only through trade by mutual consent; this gives an explicit consent boundary to the section's warning against taking by force. | terra: The ban on consuming one another's wealth makes mutually willing trade, عَن تَرَاضٍ, the lawful alternative; it supplies the consent that the section sets opposite forced taking.
luna: Oppressed men, women, and children pray to be brought out of a town and given a protector and helper; this makes shelter a response to domination, as in the section's vulnerable figures.

luna: The speakers ask to have fighting deferred to a near term, then are told worldly enjoyment is little and the Hereafter better; this joins postponement to the value of what comes after. | terra: Those who ask to be deferred to a near term are answered that worldly enjoyment is little and the Hereafter better; it is the section's exact postponement-and-better-end meeting.
luna: The verse commands justice toward orphan girls and other vulnerable children; it extends the section's orphan-care rule to a specific household vulnerability.
luna: Public mention of evil is disliked except by one who has been wronged; this marks a boundary between harmful disclosure and the section's positive telling of blessing.

luna: God guides seekers of His pleasure through paths of peace, brings them from darkness into light, and guides them to a straight path; light and direction meet in one claim. | terra: God guides seekers of His pleasure to paths of peace, brings them from darkness into light, and guides to a straight path; light and road are explicitly one guidance movement.
luna: Moses reminds Israel that God appointed prophets, made them rulers, and gave what was not given others; this is a specific act of recounting past blessing.

luna: A crow shows Cain how to conceal his brother's corpse in the earth; this is the Qur'an's concrete burial scene behind the section's covered-dead image. | terra: The raven scratches the earth to show Cain how to cover his brother's corpse; this is the section's deepest funeral detail in its literal Qur'anic scene of earth and covering.

luna: God is called الْقَاهِرُ فوق عباده, the subduer over His servants; the section names قهر as power-taking and contrasts God's sovereignty with a human's forbidden domination of an orphan. | terra: وَهُوَ ٱلْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِۦ locates irresistible qahr above all servants, clarifying why a servant may not enact downward qahr upon an orphan.
luna: God takes people by night, knows what they do by day, then awakens them for a term; this joins night, sleep-like concealment, and return.
terra: The repeated وَهُوَ ٱلْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِۦ accompanies divine guardians and the taking of souls, reserving ultimate “above” qahr to the Lord rather than a human over the weak.
terra: A person made alive after death is given a light by which to walk among people, opposite one trapped in darkness; new life, visibility, and traversable way meet exactly.

terra: Kindness to parents is followed by a ban on killing children from poverty because God provides for both generations; nurture, vulnerable children, fear of want, and divine sufficiency are joined.

luna: The command forbids approaching an orphan's property except in the best manner until maturity; it makes the section's protection a concrete limit on power. | terra: Orphan property may be approached only in the best way until maturity; it draws a firm boundary around the guardian's stronger hand.
luna: After Adam and his wife eat, they become exposed and cover themselves with leaves; this repeats the section's garden fall while making exposure and covering explicit.
luna: Adam and his wife confess that they wronged themselves and ask for forgiveness and mercy; their plea joins being lost to the need for a merciful return.
luna: The couple are sent down to earth, where they will live for a time; this shows the move from the protected garden to a bounded earthly life.
luna: God says people will live on earth, die there, and be brought out from it; the verse joins earthly dwelling, burial, and new creation.
terra: Pharaoh threatens to cut the believers' hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify them; his qahr descends literally upon hands and bodies that will not yield consent.
terra: Pharaoh's chiefs propose killing sons and sparing women, and he boasts وَإِنَّا فَوْقَهُمْ قَـٰهِرُونَ; human qahr “above them” is staged as murderous imitation of divine sovereignty.
luna: Each Israelite group receives a known drinking place, shade from clouds, and food; this brings water, shelter, and provision together in Moses's history.

luna: Believers are reminded that they were few, afraid, sheltered, strengthened, and provided good things so they might be grateful; past protection becomes an ethical memory. | terra: A formerly weak and fearful community is told to remember how God sheltered, supported, and provided for it so that it might be grateful; remembered refuge and sufficiency become an obligation to respond.

luna: The section links its source word عَائِل to need and future relief; this verse says fear of عَيْلَة (poverty) is answered by God's future enrichment. | terra: Fear of poverty, عَيْلَةً, is answered by a future promise, فَسَوْفَ يُغْنِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ; this is the section's exact meeting of delay and sufficiency.

terra: Being content with what God and His messenger give is coupled to confidence that God will give again from His bounty; the verse gathers gift, رضوا, future provision, and sufficiency in one response.
luna: God invites people to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path; this joins the section's shelter, path, and guidance in one statement.
terra: God makes night for rest and day giving sight; darkness and visibility are complementary provisions rather than abandonment and return.
terra: Joseph's brothers claim that they left the child with their belongings and a wolf ate him; it supplies the reported loss and failed human guardianship preceding the caravan's find in 12:19.
terra: The false blood on Joseph's shirt confronts Jacob with the claimed loss, and he turns to beautiful patience and God's help; the parent-owner side of the lost-child scene is made explicit.

luna: A water drawer discovers Joseph in a well and calls him good news, a boy; this repeats the section's found-and-rescued child image in another Qur'anic story. | terra: A caravan's water-drawer brings up Joseph and announces a boy, then the finders conceal him as merchandise; a lost child is “found” while his true belonging is ignored.

luna: Joseph's buyer tells his wife to give the boy an honorable home, perhaps adopting him; the household's welcome closely echoes Moses being taken in. | terra: The Egyptian buyer tells his wife to honor Joseph's lodging and perhaps adopt him, while God establishes him and teaches him; the found child receives a house and gradual formation.
terra: Joseph refuses the coercive invitation by saying his rabb/master has made his lodging good; the human-master sense of رب appears inside the lost child's shelter story.
terra: In prison Joseph asks whether scattered human lords are better than God, the One, the Overpowering; the owner sense of rabb and absolute qahr are distinguished within the found child's story.
terra: Jacob sends his sons to search attentively for Joseph and his brother and forbids despair of God's relief; it supplies the searching owner-parent side of a long-lost person's recovery.

terra: Joseph's brothers come in family hardship with poor merchandise and ask him to complete their measure and give charity; the still-unrecognized lost brother now occupies the giving side before needy askers.
terra: Joseph responds to their plea by asking whether they know what they did to Joseph and his brother; the giver's voice opens recognition rather than rebuking their need.
terra: Recognition follows, and Joseph attributes the outcome to God's favor upon him and his brother; the found one explicitly narrates the favor that enabled him to provide.
terra: Joseph, once the lost child given lodging, takes his parents into his own shelter, آوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَبَوَيْهِ; the sheltered one has become the shelterer.
terra: Joseph recounts his Lord's past kindness in release and family reunion after drawing his parents near; a completed life sequence is turned into spoken divine favor.
terra: The argument against rival lords culminates in God as the One, the Overpowering; it ties the owner sense of rabb to the unique bearer of absolute qahr.
terra: Revelation brings people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission and onto His path; the Lord makes both sight and road possible.

luna: Moses is sent to bring his people from darkness into light and remind them of God's days; this joins the section's path and light images within Moses's own story. | terra: Moses is commanded to bring his people from darkness into light and remind them of God's days; the Moses story, illumination, and spoken remembrance of favor meet in a single commission.
terra: Moses enacts that commission by telling his people to remember God's favor in rescuing them from Pharaoh's slaughter of their sons; delivered dependents become hearers of narrated favor.

luna: Moses tells his people that gratitude for God's favor brings increase; the verse gives a direct response to the section's command to speak of the Lord's blessing. | terra: Gratitude for divine favor is promised increase, while ingratitude has consequence; it gives ethical force to speaking and acknowledging the Lord's gift.
terra: When earth and heavens are replaced, all emerge before God, the One, the Overpowering; renewed creation exposes every creature to the qahr that belongs uniquely to God.
luna: God points out the straight way, while some ways bend; this makes the section's guidance image a distinction between routes, not just a change of light.
luna: Every blessing people have is from God, and in distress they call upon Him; this states the source of the favors the section tells its audience to recount.
terra: A powerless owned servant is contrasted with one granted good provision who spends from it secretly and openly; received sufficiency is made visible through free giving.
luna: What people possess comes to an end, while what is with God remains; the verse states the passing-and-enduring relation behind the section's time meeting.
terra: A secure town receiving abundant provision answers ingratitude with an encompassing taste of hunger and fear; provision once hidden by familiarity becomes perceptible through its reversal.

luna: Night and day are made signs, with the night darkened and the day made visible for seeking provision; this ties concealment, light, and sufficiency. | terra: Night and day are two signs: the night sign is effaced and the day sign made visible so people may seek bounty and reckon years; covering, visible road, provision, and time meet in one ayah.
luna: The one who wants the immediate life receives only what God wills of it and then faces an appointed end; this sets a boundary around the section's promised future giving.
luna: The one who seeks the Hereafter and strives for it is promised appreciated effort; this develops the section's contrast between the first and what follows.

luna: The section identifies تَنْهَرْ as the Qur'anic verb for rebuking; here it is forbidden toward parents and replaced by noble speech, the exact sound contrast. | terra: The only other Qur'anic prohibition with تَنْهَرْ pairs “do not rebuke them” with “say to them a noble word”; it states the gentle voice that replaces the section's forbidden voice.

luna: The next verse asks for mercy for parents as they raised the speaker young (رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا); it supplies the nurturing memory behind 17:23's gentle speech. | terra: The prayer كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا makes having been raised the reason for merciful humility, just as the section turns remembered nurture into a duty toward the vulnerable.

luna: The verse orders giving the needy and traveler their due; it names the same vulnerable recipient class whose asking the section says not to rebuke. | terra: The relative, needy person, and traveler are each to be given their due; the command turns received provision outward toward dependent and road-bound people.

luna: If the speaker must turn away while awaiting mercy, the command is to use gentle words; this gives the exact response when a request cannot be met. | terra: If one must turn away while awaiting future mercy from one's Lord, one must still speak a gentle word; deferred provision is joined directly to non-rebuking speech.
terra: The hand must be neither chained to the neck nor wholly outstretched; this gives a bodily measure to the giving hand in the surrounding needy-person passage.
terra: The Lord expands and measures provision with full knowledge of His servants; it names the divine provision behind both present inability and hoped-for future giving in 17:28.
terra: The ban on killing children for fear of poverty is grounded in God's provision for them and their parents; fear of insufficiency may not authorize qahr over a dependent child.

luna: The orphan's property may be approached only in the best way until maturity; the following command to fulfill covenants makes protection a kept trust. | terra: The same orphan-property limit is joined to fulfilling covenants; guardianship is accountable stewardship rather than ownership.
luna: People ask whether they will be raised after becoming bones and fragments; this names the corpse's apparent finality.
luna: They are told that even if they became stone or iron, God could restore them; this answers 17:49's objection to return.
luna: When they ask who will bring them back, the answer is the One who created them first; this completes the challenge with the first creation as proof.
terra: On the day God calls, the buried answer with praise and realize they stayed only a little; voice, glorification, time, and renewed emergence converge.
luna: The youths take shelter in a cave and ask their Lord for mercy and right guidance in their affair; it brings shelter, asking, and direction together.
luna: The youths are told to withdraw to the cave, trusting God to spread mercy and prepare ease; this develops the refuge and guidance petition in 18:10.
terra: Moses declares that he will keep traveling until he reaches the meeting of the two seas; purposeful seeking opens a journey whose lost sign will lead him to a guide.
terra: At the meeting place Moses and his servant lose track of their fish as it takes its path into the sea; losing the object marks the place they were seeking.
terra: The servant remembers the forgotten fish and its astonishing path at the rock; the forgotten loss becomes articulated guidance back to the meeting place.
terra: Moses says “that is what we were seeking” and they retrace their footprints; search, recovery, and a road reversed join in one action.
terra: They find a servant given mercy and taught knowledge by God; the journey's lost sign ends in finding the human guide.
terra: Moses asks to follow the found servant so that he may be taught some of the guidance given him; the former guide takes the position of a traveler asking for guidance.
terra: In a town that refuses hospitality, the two travelers find and repair a collapsing wall without payment; the visible unpaid act conceals the orphan protection explained in 18:82.
terra: The damaged boat belongs to poor workers, and the hidden act protects it from a king who seizes every sound boat by force; unseen care frustrates a ruler's coercive taking from the poor.

luna: A wall is repaired to protect the treasure of two orphan boys until maturity because their father was righteous; this makes hidden provision and a guardian's care literal. | terra: A wall preserves treasure for two orphan boys until they reach maturity, because their father was righteous and their Lord willed mercy; unseen guardianship protects the orphan's future property.
terra: The human is told to remember that God created him before when he was nothing; it states the section's “what was not becomes” layer of new creation.

luna: Moses sees a fire while traveling with his family and hopes to bring back news or a brand; this is the section's fire as a possible guide. | terra: Moses sees a fire from afar and hopes either for a brand or أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى; a visible light becomes the hoped-for place of finding guidance.
luna: As Moses approaches the fire, he is called by name; this neighboring call resolves the search for guidance begun in 20:10.
luna: Moses says he leans on his staff and beats down leaves for his sheep; this gives a second concrete pastoral scene beside his encounter with the women's flock.
terra: Moses begins the request granted in 20:36 by asking his Lord to expand his breast; the inward heart-side of the coming speech mission is named.
terra: He asks his Lord to ease his task; this identifies the requested ease to which the divine grant in 20:36 responds.
terra: He asks that the knot in his tongue be loosened; voice itself is one of the needs met before he must address Pharaoh.
terra: Moses asks that people understand his speech; the purpose of the loosened tongue is communicative reception, not domination by voice.
terra: Moses asks for help so that he and Aaron may glorify God much; the granted request is directed toward spoken remembrance.
terra: He adds that they may remember God much; remembrance answers the earlier favors that God begins recounting in 20:37.
terra: قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ answers Moses's request before recounting earlier favors, matching the section's movement from a granted desire to remembered gift.

luna: God recalls that He had already favored Moses once before (مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰ); the section reads Moses's later provision as part of a remembered history of gifts. | terra: God explicitly narrates an earlier favor to Moses, وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰ, enacting the section's command to bring a Lord-given favor into speech.

luna: The account turns to what was revealed to Moses's mother; this begins the infant's hidden passage from danger toward shelter described in the section. | terra: The earlier favor begins with revelation to Moses's mother; this row supplies the divine initiative whose concrete instructions continue in 20:39.

luna: The child is placed in a chest and cast into the river, yet God says He put love on Moses and that he would be raised under His eye; danger becomes guarded nurture. | terra: The infant is cast into the chest and river, taken by an enemy, covered with divine love, and reared under God's eye; exposure, apparent loss, ownership, and nurture meet here.

luna: Moses's sister offers someone to care for him, and he is returned to his mother for her eye to be cooled; this completes the shelter-and-reunion sequence. | terra: Moses's sister leads to a carer, he is returned so his mother's eye may be comforted, rescued after killing a man, tried, and brought from Midian “according to a measure”; it compresses the section's shelter-road-provision life sequence.

luna: God says He chose Moses for Himself; this follows the rescued childhood and makes the later guidance part of a sustained favor. | terra: وَٱصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِى completes the infant's being fashioned under God's eye by naming the Lord's deliberate forming and choosing of him.

luna: Moses and Aaron are told to speak gently to Pharaoh; even in a difficult encounter, the Qur'an makes softness of voice the chosen way. | terra: Moses and Aaron are commanded to speak gently even to Pharaoh; soft speech is required in the very encounter with the human imitator of qahr.

luna: Human beings are made from earth, returned to it, and brought out again; the verse joins burial and emergence in one sequence. | terra: Humans are created from earth, returned to it, and brought out from it once more; burial becomes the middle movement between two creations.
terra: Pharaoh repeats the threat to sever hands and feet and crucify the magicians for believing without his permission; he treats inward assent as property under his command.
luna: The section places Adam in a garden before the fall; this neighboring promise names freedom from hunger, nakedness, and thirst, completing the protected setting that 20:119 adds to.

luna: The section links its source root ض ح و to a road appearing in daylight; Adam is promised he will not be exposed to its heat (تَضْحَىٰ), making dawn a form of protection. | terra: Adam is promised that he will not suffer the sun's exposed heat, וَلَا تَضْحَىٰ; this supplies the section's exact meeting of ḍuḥā exposure with the story of losing and receiving guidance.

luna: The tempter promises Adam a tree of lasting life and a kingdom that will not decay; this false promise of permanence sharpens the section's distinction between what is promised and what truly endures.
luna: After eating, Adam and his wife cover themselves with garden leaves; this is the fall's immediate exposure-and-covering scene, before guidance follows in 20:122.

luna: After Adam's lapse, his Lord chooses him, accepts his repentance, and guides him; this directly joins a fall to the return and guidance the section pairs. | terra: After Adam's fall, his Lord chooses him, turns to him, and guides him; this is the section's sequence of a dependent person being reclaimed and led.

luna: The section's lost path is answered by Adam's promise: whoever follows God's guidance will not go astray or be wretched, specifying what guidance secures. | terra: The descent is followed by promised guidance, and whoever follows it فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ; loss of way and relief from misery meet exactly as the section describes.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord before sunrise, before sunset, and through parts of night so that he may be satisfied; light-times, speech, رب, and رضا meet.
luna: The Prophet is told not to strain his eyes toward worldly splendor, since his Lord's provision is better and more lasting; it joins provision with the section's future-facing measure.
terra: David and Solomon judge a field into which a people's sheep strayed by night; night, an uncontrolled herd, ownership, and responsibility meet in one legal scene.
terra: God makes Solomon understand the judgment and gives both prophets wisdom; divine guidance resolves the night-herd dispute introduced in 21:78.

luna: The verse traces human formation through the womb and compares revival to barren earth stirred by rain; it makes new creation visible in body and land. | terra: Human formation from dust through measured womb stages and the revival of barren earth are offered as evidence of resurrection; growth, nurture, earth, and new creation form one argument.
luna: The Hour is certain and God will raise those in the graves; this directly joins the section's buried body to its new creation.
luna: After the described stages of human creation, the verse says people will surely die; it names the death that the section's grave image covers.
luna: The next verse says people will be raised on the Resurrection Day; it completes 23:15's death with return.

luna: Marriage is encouraged even for the poor, with God's promise to enrich them from His bounty; this directly joins Moses's marriage to the section's passage from need to sufficiency. | terra: The unmarried are to be married, and if they are poor God will enrich them from His bounty; marriage and household become the promised route from poverty to sufficiency, as in Moses's Midian scene.
terra: Those unable to marry remain chaste until God enriches them from His bounty; delayed household and delayed sufficiency are held together.
terra: Layered darkness leaves a person scarcely able to see his own hand, and one denied God's light has no light; it gives the section's hand image a concrete boundary of invisibility.

luna: Night is made a garment and sleep a rest, while day is made for rising; it gives covering and emergence distinct functions. | terra: God makes night a covering, sleep a rest, and day a rising; the section's cover-light movement deepens into a daily image of death and renewed emergence.
luna: Believers ask for spouses and children as قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ, comfort to their eyes; the phrase echoes the section's child returned so his mother's eye may be cooled.

luna: Pharaoh claims, 'Did we not raise you among us as a child?'; the section explicitly hears رب as owner and nurturer, while this is Pharaoh's human claim to have raised Moses. | terra: Pharaoh's أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا uses the nurture branch of رب while claiming ownership of the child raised in his house.
terra: Pharaoh calls Moses's former deed ingratitude immediately after claiming to have raised him; human nurture is weaponized as a debt and accusation.

luna: Moses describes his earlier self as among the ضَّالِّين; the section explicitly links ض ل ل to one who does not know which way to turn, so his words carry the lost-way sense. | terra: Moses describes his former state as وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ; in context it is the unknowing state from which flight, judgment, and mission follow.

luna: After Moses says he fled in fear, he says his Lord gave him judgment and made him a messenger; it extends the section's lost-to-guided sequence in Moses's own account. | terra: Moses answers that he fled in fear, then his Lord gave him judgment and made him a messenger; the coercive household's claim is displaced by the true Lord's rescue and gift.
terra: Moses rejects Pharaoh's claimed “favor” because Pharaoh enslaved the Children of Israel; it is the boundary between narrating divine favor and using a supposed gift to erase oppression.
terra: The same threat follows Pharaoh's demand that belief require his permission; coercive rule attempts to seize both bodily hands and the heart's رضا.

luna: Moses tells his family to wait as he sees fire and hopes to bring news or a burning brand; the same distant light is treated as a practical guide. | terra: In the third telling, Moses sees a fire from afar and tells his family he may bring news or a burning brand so they can warm themselves; road information and useful light are again sought together.
luna: At the fire Moses is called and the presence is blessed; this next step supplies a speaker for the light he had approached in 27:7.
terra: Solomon asks his Lord to enable gratitude for favors granted to him and his parents and to make him act rightly; inherited nurture and divine gift are converted into word and deed.
terra: After the throne is brought, Solomon calls it his Lord's bounty and a test of gratitude; an accomplished gift is immediately and openly attributed to its true giver.

luna: Pharaoh divides the people, oppresses a group, and kills their sons; this is the human domination of the vulnerable that the section sets against the command not to crush an orphan. | terra: Pharaoh exalts himself, divides the people, and slaughters sons while sparing women; the ruler turns power over dependent children into corruption rather than shelter.
luna: God promises to favor those oppressed in the land and make them leaders and inheritors; the reversal answers Pharaoh's domination with protection and elevation.

luna: Moses's mother is told to nurse him, cast him into the river if afraid, and not fear because he will be returned; this joins vulnerability, shelter, and promised guidance. | terra: Moses's mother is told to nurse him, cast him into the river when afraid, and trust the promise of return; loss, provision, protection, and future restoration occupy one command.

luna: Pharaoh's household retrieves the child, though he is to become their enemy and grief; the section's sheltering image is shadowed by the danger of a protector's house. | terra: Pharaoh's household picks up the exposed infant, placing the found child inside the very house that will oppose him; it supplies the dangerous human “finder” in the continuing rescue scene.

luna: Pharaoh's wife calls the child an eye's comfort, asks that he not be killed, and proposes adoption; this is a ruler's household sheltering an abandoned infant. | terra: Pharaoh's wife calls the found infant a comfort to the eye and proposes taking him as a son; the apparently ownerless child is offered a household and protection from killing.

luna: Moses's mother's heart empties and she nearly discloses him; this is a precise instance of the section's movement between concealment and telling. | terra: Moses's mother's heart becomes empty and nearly discloses him until God binds her heart; the verse gives the inward cost of the loss whose outward search continues in 28:11.

luna: Moses's sister watches him from a distance; her watching leads to the offer of a nursing household in 28:12. | terra: The mother tells Moses's sister to follow him, and she watches from afar without being recognized; this is the searching side of the section's lost-and-finder pair.

luna: The sister offers to direct Pharaoh's household to a family who will care for the infant; this is the specific household shelter the section describes. | terra: After other nurses are withheld, the sister offers to show a household that will care sincerely for the child; guidance, household, and nurture become the means of finding his proper carer.

luna: Moses is returned to his mother so her eye may be cooled and she not grieve; this completes the protection promised in 28:7. | terra: God returns Moses to his mother so her eye is comforted and she knows the promise is true; the lost infant is found, housed, and restored to رضا-like relief.
luna: When Moses reaches maturity, God grants him judgment and knowledge; the verse supplies the growth from a cared-for child to an adult that the section's nurturing image implies.
luna: Moses finds two men fighting, one asks his help, and Moses strikes the other; the verse supplies the earlier crisis behind his later description of himself as lost.
luna: Moses asks forgiveness for wronging himself and is forgiven; this makes his later flight and guidance part of a received mercy.
luna: Moses says that because God favored him he will not support wrongdoers; this explicitly turns remembered favor into an ethic, as the section's commands do.
luna: Moses flees the city in fear and asks his Lord to save him from wrongdoing people; this begins the path to Midian as a search for safety.

luna: Fleeing toward Midian, Moses asks his Lord to guide him to the sound way (يَهْدِيَنِي سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ); the path in the section is here an urgent request. | terra: On setting out toward Midian, Moses says that perhaps his Lord will guide him to the level way; the traveler who does not know his route asks رب for direction.

luna: Moses finds (وَوَجَدَ) two women holding back their flock while others water theirs; the verse joins the section's finding verb to its meeting of path and herd. | terra: At Midian's water Moses finds two women holding back their flock while the other herders water, and learns that their father is old; finding, herd, vulnerable dependents, and absent shepherd meet visibly.

luna: After watering the women's flock, Moses withdraws to shade and says he needs whatever good his Lord sends; the scene makes shelter and provision meet in one prayer. | terra: Moses waters the women's flock, withdraws to shade, and confesses to his Lord that he is فقير for whatever good is sent; the helper stands at once on the giving and needy sides of the section's scene.

luna: The daughter walks modestly to invite Moses to her father; this is the welcome at home that follows his help at the well in 28:24. | terra: One woman returns modestly with a father's invitation to reward Moses for watering, and the father gives him safety; provision for an act of care becomes admission into a protective household.

luna: The father is told to hire Moses because he is strong and trustworthy; the verse turns shelter into a dependable place and livelihood. | terra: The daughter recommends employing Moses as strong and trustworthy; this verse supplies the judgment that turns the unprovided traveler into a supported member of the household.

luna: The father offers Moses marriage to one of his daughters after his service; this is the household and marriage the section names in its life sequence. | terra: The father offers one of his daughters in marriage in exchange for a fixed term of service; the lost and poor traveler is given family, home, and measured livelihood.

luna: The marriage offer is fixed to an eight- or ten-year term, with no injustice in the agreement; it makes the section's deferred time concrete inside Moses's new household. | terra: Moses accepts either measured term without injustice and makes God trustee over the agreement; it makes consent, limit, and divine oversight explicit in the new household.

luna: After the term, Moses travels with his family and sees a fire, hoping for news or a burning brand; it is the section's distant fire that may offer direction and warmth. | terra: After completing the term, Moses travels with his family and sees a fire, hoping for news or a brand; completed provision leads back to the light-at-a-distance road scene.
luna: The next verse calls Moses from the side of the valley at the fire; it supplies the voice and divine direction that the preceding fire-seeking scene has not yet revealed.
luna: What people are given is only the adornment of worldly life, while what is with God is better and lasting; this gives a concrete form to what passes and remains.

luna: God asks who could bring light if night were made perpetual; this states the boundary of the section's movement from covering to visible guidance. | terra: A perpetual night is posed as a world in which no other god can bring light; the question makes visible light a divine provision, continued by the night-day purposes in 28:73.

luna: God asks who could bring night if day were made perpetual; the paired reversal completes 28:71's contrast between darkness and light. | terra: A perpetual day is posed against the night in which people rest; it gives the necessary limit to exposure before 28:73 reunites rest and provision.

luna: By mercy God made night for rest and day for seeking bounty; this joins covering and provision as the section's paired night and daylight do. | terra: Night for rest and day for seeking God's bounty are named together as mercy; covering and light become complementary forms of provision.
luna: Qarun is told to seek the Hereafter with what God gave him and to do good as God did good to him; this states the return from received blessing to care for others.

luna: God brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, then gives life to earth after its death; this states both reversals in the section's buried-life image. | terra: God brings living from dead and dead from living and revives earth after death; emergence from burial is placed within a recurring reversal.
terra: Heaven and earth stand by God's command, then one call brings people out of the earth; divine voice turns the earth-covered dead into a new emergence.
luna: The verse points to the earth revived after its death and says the same God will revive the dead; it makes renewal visible in the land.
luna: Human life moves from weakness to strength and back to weakness and age; this renders the section's claim that the Lord carries a person from state to state.
terra: The human is charged to thank God and parents after recalling the mother's weakness and two years of nurture; remembered raising is converted into grateful conduct.
luna: A reward hidden from people is called قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ; this joins the section's hidden blessing and eye-comfort language.
terra: God and His angels bless believers in order to bring them from darkness into light; divine care is expressed as illumination rather than abandonment.
terra: All people are the poor before God while God alone is the self-sufficient, praiseworthy one; it keeps human enrichment from becoming imagined independence.
luna: The sign is that daylight is stripped from night, leaving people in darkness; it states the visible world as a boundary between light and concealment.
luna: The challenge asks who can give life to bones after they have decayed; it names the very corpse that seems beyond return.
luna: The answer is that the One who produced life the first time will revive it; this completes the decayed-bone question with new creation.
terra: The owner of ninety-nine ewes demands the other man's single ewe and overpowers him in speech; flock, taking without رضا, and coercive voice meet in one counter-scene.
terra: David identifies the demand for the single ewe as injustice and generalizes that partners often transgress; judgment sets a limit on the stronger owner's grasp.
terra: The person whose breast God opens is upon light from his Lord, opposite hard hearts; inward softness and outward light define receptivity to guidance.
terra: At the best discourse, skins shiver and then skins and hearts soften to God's remembrance, and this is called God's guidance; speech, softness, heart, and guidance meet.
luna: God takes souls at death and during sleep, retaining some and sending others back until a term; this connects the night's covering to the grave's return.
terra: When all are brought forth with nothing hidden, the question of dominion is answered: it belongs to God, the One, the Overpowering; exposure after death and ultimate qahr coincide.
terra: Night is made for rest and day as something visible, and the arrangement is called divine bounty; light-dark alternation itself is narrated as favor.
luna: Human life is traced from dust and stages in the womb through childhood, maturity, and old age; this makes the section's nurturing from state to state a broader human pattern.

luna: Revelation is made a light by which God guides, and the verse ends with guidance to a straight path; it brings the section's light and road into a single image. | terra: The Prophet did not know the Book or faith, then revelation became a light by which God guides, and he guides to a straight path; this joins the section's prophetic addressee, light, and guidance without implying culpable error.

terra: After recalling pregnancy, birth, and growth to maturity, the adult asks to thank God for favors to him and his parents and to act rightly; nurture culminates in spoken gratitude and outward duty.
terra: People are invited to spend, yet some withhold; God is the rich one and they are the poor, reversing any claim that the giver owns sufficiency in himself.

luna: This verse joins completion of a blessing to guidance on a straight path; it is the section's explicit meeting of sufficiency and being led. | terra: God's completing His favor to the Prophet and guiding him on a straight path, وَيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ ... وَيَهْدِيَكَ, directly joins completed gift to guidance.
luna: The pledge is made by believers' hands beneath God's hand; as a willing covenant, it contrasts the section's coercive hand that takes without consent.

luna: The verse assigns a right in wealth to the asker and the deprived; it makes the needy person's claim part of provision, not an intrusion. | terra: The wealthy acknowledge in their property a right for both the asker and the deprived; the asking voice calls forth a due rather than a rebuke.

luna: The verse says God is the One who enriches (أَغْنَىٰ); it names the same specific change from need to sufficiency that the section recalls in 93:8. | terra: وَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ identifies God as the one who enriches and grants sufficiency, reinforcing the true source behind the section's passive receipt.
luna: God is named the First and Last, the Manifest and Hidden; this brings the section's after/first and concealment/disclosure pairings into one statement.
terra: Clear signs are sent down to the servant so that God may bring people from darkness into light; the prophetic recipient becomes the means of others' illumination.
terra: The Helpers give preference to others despite their own need and feel no inward want over what others receive; scarcity, رضا, and outward generosity are reconciled.
luna: For one mindful of God, He makes a way out; the neighboring promise in 65:3 adds unexpected provision, joining the section's road and sufficiency.
luna: God provides from where a person does not expect and is sufficient for whoever trusts Him; this completes 65:2's way out with provision.

terra: Divorced women must be housed according to means without harmful pressure, supported through pregnancy, paid for nursing, and treated through fitting consultation; shelter, provision, nurture, and consent displace coercion.

luna: A person with ample means is to spend accordingly and one with restricted provision according to what God gave; the verse promises ease after hardship, joining giving, need, and delay. | terra: Each person spends according to means, including one whose provision is measured tightly, and God promises ease after hardship; provision received sets the measure of provision given.
terra: The messenger recites clear signs to bring believers from darkness into light, after which righteous action receives a good provision; illumination and provision form one guided movement.

luna: The next ayah says the believers' wealth contains a known right; this establishes the share whose recipients are named in 70:25. | terra: Those who pray assign a recognized share in their wealth; 70:25 names the asker and deprived as its owners.

luna: The right belongs to the asker and the deprived; this completes 70:24 and makes the section's petitioner a recognized recipient. | terra: The assigned share belongs to the asker and the deprived; this turns response to need from discretionary favor into acknowledged right.

luna: Human beings are said to grow from the earth like plants; this gives the section's new creation a specific image of emergence. | terra: God causes humanity to grow from the earth like a growth; the nurturing image is extended into bodily creation from soil.

luna: The next verse says people return to the earth and are brought forth again; it completes the planting image with burial and resurrection. | terra: He then returns people to the earth and brings them out again; the covered dead becomes a renewed emergence.
luna: The doubter asks whether God can gather his bones; this names the bodily obstacle raised against the section's promise of renewed creation.
luna: The answer says God can restore even fingertips; this completes 75:3 by specifying the body's reassembly.
terra: People love the immediate life, ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ, making haste rather than deferred good their governing desire.
terra: They leave the Hereafter, the direct reversal of the section's claim that the later is better.
terra: A span of time passed when the human was not a thing mentioned; nonexistence, time, and eventual mention meet the section's “becoming” and speaking images.

luna: The righteous give food to the needy, orphan, and captive despite loving it; this makes care an actual transfer to the vulnerable. | terra: They feed the poor, orphan, and captive despite loving or needing the food; provision is passed onward without waiting for abundance.

luna: They explain that they feed only for God's countenance and want neither repayment nor thanks; this states the motive behind 76:8's giving. | terra: They say they seek neither repayment nor thanks from recipients; the giving hand renounces the coercive claim that a favor creates.

luna: This verse asks whether the earth was made a container (كِفَاتًا); 77:26 names its contents, the living and the dead, grounding the section's burial image. | terra: The earth is called a containing vessel; 77:26 states that it contains both living and dead, matching the section's shelter-cover transition.

luna: This verse names the living and the dead as earth's contents; 77:25 calls the earth a container, making the section's covered-body image a shared human condition. | terra: The earth contains the living and the dead; home and grave become two uses of the same sheltering ground.

luna: Night is called a covering; this states directly the concealment half of the section's light meeting. | terra: Night is made a garment, a compact image of the covering that the section hears in night.

luna: Day is made for livelihood; the following verse links the covering night to provision in daylight. | terra: Day is made a time of livelihood, joining visible day to the provision for which people go out.
terra: The Prophet's frown and turning away stage the rebuff that the section's command forbids; 80:2 identifies the vulnerable person who approached.
terra: The reason for the rebuff is that the blind man came to him; this verse supplies the dependent seeker in the corrected encounter.
terra: The addressee is reminded that the seeker may purify himself; it reveals what a harsh reception could withhold from the one who came.
terra: The seeker may remember and benefit from the reminder; the proper answer to his approach is useful speech, not dismissal.
terra: The person who considers himself self-sufficient, ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ, receives attention; this is the wrongly favored pole opposite the dependent seeker.
terra: The Prophet is reproved for attending to the self-sufficient person; it reverses the section's priority toward the one who comes in need.
terra: The addressee is not responsible if that self-sufficient person does not purify himself; the verse removes the rationale for neglecting the vulnerable seeker.
terra: The one who comes striving is set opposite the person treated as self-sufficient; his active approach sharpens the section's responsibility toward a sāʾil.
terra: The approaching person also fears God; this makes his outward dependence carry inward moral seriousness.
terra: The rebuke is that the addressee is distracted from the striving, fearful seeker; it is a direct prophetic correction of turning away.

luna: The human is caused to die and buried; this is the section's covered body in the earth. | terra: God causes the human to die and assigns him a grave; it supplies the section's covered and earth-given corpse.

luna: The next verse says the human will be raised when God wills; it completes burial with new creation. | terra: Then, whenever He wills, God raises that human; the grave of 80:21 opens onto new creation rather than abandonment.
terra: The girl buried alive is asked a question on the final day; the covered, powerless child is restored as the addressed party rather than the object of another's qahr.
terra: She is asked for what sin she was killed; resurrection exposes and judges the ultimate coercion against a dependent child.
terra: God measures and then guides, وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ; fitted measure and direction are two aspects of the Lord's ordering.
terra: God knows what is made public and what is hidden; this supplies the epistemic boundary behind the section's movement from covering to telling.
terra: God promises the prophetic addressee facilitation toward ease; it parallels the section's future promise without repeating its gift language.

luna: People are said to prefer the nearer life; this is the choice opposite the section's claim that what comes after is better. | terra: People prefer the nearer worldly life; this names the preference corrected by the section's “the later is better.”

luna: The Hereafter is called better and more enduring than the worldly life, giving the section's after/first contrast its direct Qur'anic formulation. | terra: وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ states both the greater worth and greater endurance of the later life.
terra: A person interprets expanded provision as “my Lord has honored me”; the verse opens the false equation between wealth and divine regard that 89:16-18 overturn.
terra: When provision is measured tightly, the same person says “my Lord has humiliated me”; this exposes the felt humiliation of poverty before the orphan commands correct the diagnosis.

luna: The passage rebukes people for failing to honor the orphan; it names the opposite conduct to the section's command. | terra: The response “No” is followed by the charge that they do not honor the orphan; true reception of divine provision is measured by treatment of the dependent.

luna: The next verse reproaches them for not urging one another to feed the poor; it completes the orphan-and-need pairing with shared responsibility. | terra: They do not urge one another to feed the poor; the verse converts the mistaken wealth judgment into the same duty toward need found in the section.

luna: They are accused of consuming inheritance greedily; this is a concrete form of taking from those whose property should be protected. | terra: They consume inheritance with devouring greed after failing the orphan and poor; the taking hand is shown at its harshest.

luna: This verse itself says people love wealth fiercely; beside 89:19's charge of devouring inheritance, that desire is the appetite opposed to the section's provision and restraint. | terra: Their excessive love of wealth names the heart-state behind withholding and devouring, opposite رضا with what the Lord gives.
terra: The person has not attempted the steep path; the road image becomes a moral passage whose concrete acts toward captives, orphans, and the poor follow.

luna: The surah calls a moral act the steep path; the following verses define it through freeing and feeding, meeting the section's path image with its care commands. | terra: “What will make you know what the steep path is?” announces that the following care acts define the path rather than merely ornament it.

luna: The first deed on that steep path is freeing a neck; this adds release from domination to the section's prohibition on crushing. | terra: Freeing a neck is the first act that crosses the steep path, reversing domination by releasing the person under another's power.
luna: The path next requires feeding on a day of hunger; this connects guided conduct to material need. | terra: Feeding on a day of hunger makes provision in scarcity part of walking the steep path.
luna: The one fed is an orphan close in relation; this makes the section's orphan care part of the steep path. | terra: The recipient is an orphan of near kin; path and orphan-care meet explicitly.

luna: The path's next recipient is a needy person in misery; it adds the section's asker and poverty to the same moral sequence. | terra: The alternative recipient is a poor person in the dust; the path culminates in raising the lowly rather than passing over him.

luna: This oath names the day as it displays the sun; it repeats the section's visible-light side in a distinct formulation. | terra: The oath by the day إِذَا جَلَّىٰهَا makes daylight the act of disclosure, matching the section's movement from covered night to manifest gift.

luna: The paired oath names night as it covers; this repeats the concealment side of the section's night-and-light meeting. | terra: The following oath by the night إِذَا يَغْشَىٰهَا makes night a covering, the direct counterpart to 91:3's disclosure.

luna: The section names the root ل ي ل in its night image; this oath describes night as it covers, matching the covering half of the section's light-and-concealment meeting. | terra: وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ repeats the section's night-as-cover action in another oath that will lead to giving and self-sufficiency.

luna: The paired oath names daytime as it appears (النَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ); it matches the section's daylight road becoming manifest. | terra: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ answers the covering night with a day that becomes manifest, preparing the same surah's contrast between giver and self-sufficient miser.
terra: The giving sequence begins with the one who gives and is mindful; this is the active answer expected from someone who has received sufficiency.
terra: The giver confirms the best promise, supplying the trust in future good that makes giving possible.
terra: God promises to ease the giver toward ease; future divine facilitation answers the person's present act of giving.
terra: The counterfigure withholds and deems himself self-sufficient, بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ; enrichment becomes a false independence that blocks giving.
terra: He denies the best promise, reversing the giver's trust in future good.
terra: God eases the withholding, self-sufficient person toward hardship; it reverses the future ease promised to the giver.
terra: The protected person gives his wealth to purify himself; the hand enriched by God becomes a giving hand.
terra: He is not repaying a favor owed to another person; this prevents the gift from becoming a coercive human claim of ownership.
terra: He gives only seeking the face of his Lord Most High; رب and the “above” position are redirected from human domination to divine رضا.
terra: The giver will soon be satisfied, وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ; the phrase closes the giver's sequence with the same deferred رضا promised in the section.

luna: God reminds the same addressee that He expanded his breast; this opens another short surah by naming a prior favor before its ease and commands. | terra: The prophetic addressee is asked whether God expanded his breast; the adjacent reassurance begins by making an inward divine gift remembered.

luna: God recalls removing the addressee's burden; this adds a past relief to the section's remembered shelter and provision. | terra: God is recalled as removing the Prophet's burden; past relief precedes the ease promise already linked in 94:5-6.
luna: The burden had weighed upon his back; this specifies what the relief in 94:2 removed and parallels the section's movement from strain to support.

luna: God says He raised the addressee's mention; this makes the blessing publicly known, beside the section's instruction to tell of a blessing. | terra: God raises the Prophet's mention; received favor becomes public remembrance without becoming the Prophet's own coercive claim.

luna: The same addressee is promised ease with hardship; this names the relief anticipated by the section's future giving. | terra: Ease is asserted with hardship to the same prophetic addressee after remembered favors; relief is present within constriction rather than merely after it.

luna: The ease-with-hardship assurance is repeated; the repetition makes the promise firm, as the section counts both past provision and what is still to come. | terra: The repeated promise of ease stabilizes the future-facing reassurance before the following commands to act and turn to the Lord.

luna: After one task is completed, the addressee is told to strive; this continues the movement from received relief to an action that follows. | terra: When the Prophet is free, he is commanded to labor on; recalled favor and promised ease turn into action.

luna: The next command is to direct longing to the Lord; it completes 94:7's response to favor with the section's return from reminder to duty. | terra: The action culminates in directing desire toward the Lord; رب remains the owner and goal after every received gift.
terra: The human transgresses; 96:7 identifies perceived self-sufficiency as the trigger, warning what may happen after enrichment.
terra: أَن رَّءَاهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ makes seeing oneself self-sufficient the cause of overstepping, the exact moral danger when the formerly poor person stands above another.
terra: The earth casts out its burdens; what was covered and entrusted to soil becomes manifest.
terra: On that day the earth تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا, narrating its news; the section's “tell” root and grave-emergence layer meet directly.
terra: The earth narrates because its Lord has inspired it; the speech of 99:4 is explicitly grounded in رب.
terra: The people are commanded to worship the Lord of this House; rabb's owner sense and protective household are made explicit before provision is named.
terra: That Lord fed them against hunger and secured them against fear; ownership of the house is expressed through provision and refuge.

luna: The denier of judgment is identified as one who repels the orphan; this is the direct opposite of the section's command not to crush him. | terra: The denier is identified as the one who violently repels the orphan; this is the clearest enacted opposite of “do not overpower the orphan.”

luna: The same person does not urge feeding the poor; this adds a failure of mutual care beside the rebuff in 107:2. | terra: He does not urge feeding the poor; the failure toward need continues from physical repulsion into withheld provision.
